references.text: Pharaoh again asks Moses to pray to the Lord to remove a plague, this time the flies, and promises to let the people go.
Pharaoh asks Moses and Aaron to pray to the Lord to stop the hail plague, and promises to let the people of Israel go.
Pharaoh admits his sin and asks Moses to pray to the Lord to remove the locust plague.
Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let the people of Israel go to celebrate a feast for the Lord, the same demand repeated here.
The people ask Moses to intercede with the Lord to remove the snakes, similar to Pharaoh's request for intercession.
Samuel intercedes with the Lord on behalf of the people, an example of intercession that Pharaoh requests.
Simon asks the apostles to pray to the Lord for him, similar to Pharaoh's request for intercession.
The contrast between God's demand for freedom and Pharaoh's tactical offer shows Pharaoh's reluctance toward true submission.
The repeated phrasing emphasizes God's unchanging demand against Pharaoh's varying and often inadequate responses.
Both verses reveal Pharaoh's tactic of offering limited freedom to avoid complete submission.
The connection shows Pharaoh's unstable response to the plagues, where admission of sin is often replaced by new compromise attempts.
The contrast between sacrificing locally (8:21) and going out to sacrifice (8:4) shows Pharaoh's attempt to limit Israel's freedom.
Moses' warning in 8:25 refers directly to Pharaoh's promise in 8:4 and reveals his pattern of breaking his word.
Both verses show Pharaoh's persistent attempts to control who may go out to serve God, contrary to God's demand for full freedom.
